pages.text: A pilotable mech, about three and a half blocks tall: white armour with blue trim. Its trunk is a bay you stand in, back against a harness, looking out through the visor of its head. You climb in, and it walks, jumps and punches for you.

The $(item)Mech Frame$() is end-game: it is built around a $(l:mech/mech_core)Mech Core$(/l), whose crystal comes from reactor waste. Build a $(l:mech/mech_hangar)Mech Hangar$(/l) too: a frame only unfolds on a hangar's pad. Right-click the pad and the mech unfolds in the middle of it, facing out of the hangar. A new frame comes with $(l)200,000 FE$() in its
pages.title: Standing it up

pages.text: battery.$(br2)To pack it up again, park it on the pad and press $(l)Fold$() on the hangar's console: it folds itself up and drops as its frame, keeping the battery's charge and its modules.

$(li)$(l)Right-click$() the mech: it crouches a little and the front of its trunk opens like a flower, four petals swinging out one after the other while the visor plate lifts. You walk up, turn round and back into the bay, up a step; the petals close around you and the mech straightens up.
pages.title: Getting in and out

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Press V$() (the $(o)Exit mech$() key in the controls) to get out: it crouches and opens with a hiss of steam, you come off the harness, step down out of the bay and walk off, and it closes up again. Sneaking does not get you out.

$(li)$(l)W A S D$(): Walk; turn by looking around$(br)$(li)$(l)Space$(): Jump about five blocks high$(br)$(li)$(l)Left click (empty hand)$(): Punch: 10 extra damage, 100 FE$(br)$(li)$(l)Left click a block$(): Dig like an iron pickaxe, with the right drops
pages.title: Piloting

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Space in the air (Jet)$(): Climb; sneak to dive, neither to glide$(br)$(li)$(l)R / G (Drill / Blade)$(): Switch the drill or the blade on and off

The pilot reaches $(l)2.5 blocks$() further from the cockpit, and the crosshair never lands on the mech itself. Inside, you are shielded: whatever would hurt you hurts the mech instead, and neither of you takes fall damage.

In first person you look out through the visor: the mech's arms are at your sides and throw a punch when you hit, and looking down you see its legs. Press $(l)F5$() for an outside view from further back.
You hear it, too: servos and a hiss of steam as it opens, the armour locking shut, the systems booting, heavy footsteps and a thud when it lands, the jet's roar, the drill's spin and the blade's hum.

The battery holds $(l)1,000,000 FE$(). Walking uses about $(l)200 FE per block$() and the systems $(l)2 FE/t$() while you sit inside; with an empty battery the mech cannot move (you can still get out).
pages.title: Battery and integrity

pages.text: $(l)Integrity$() is the mech's health. It never blows up: when it would, it $(l)shuts down$(), slumps over and lets you out. A shut-down mech must be repaired before you can climb in again: park it in a $(l:mech/mech_hangar)Mech Hangar$(/l), which also charges its battery and fits its $(l:mech/mech_modules)modules$(/l).

While you pilot, the usual hearts, hunger and experience bar give way to the mech's display. When the cockpit closes, the systems boot with a scan of the view. Then you see:$(br)$(li)brackets in the corners and a reticle around the crosshair;
pages.title: The cockpit display

pages.text: $(li)a $(l)compass$() along the top, with your heading in degrees;$(br)$(li)$(l)ENERGY$() and $(l)INTEGRITY$() bars on the left, flashing a warning when power runs low;$(br)$(li)$(l)speed$(), $(l)altitude$() and the installed $(l)modules$() on the right.
